items.content: Synthetic ticker policy: (1) When generating a base symbol, remove leading articles, conjunction-only tokens, and corporate or legal suffixes, then concatenate the initial alphanumeric character of each remaining word in uppercase. (2) When the normalized organization name has only one substantive word, use up to its first four letters in uppercase rather than a one-letter initial. (3) Treat hyphens, apostrophes, periods, plus signs, and accented letters as normalization boundaries or removable punctuation, while preserving the initials of the resulting substantive components in transliterated uppercase form. (4) For a numeric token, preserve a compact numeric contribution—typically its first digit—alongside the initials of substantive word tokens; if a token begins with digits followed by letters, retain the leading digit as that token’s contribution. (5) Preserve meaningful uppercase initialisms embedded in a name as their constituent letters when forming the compact symbol, subject to the demonstrated overall four-character base-symbol scale. (6) When a name ends with “Class X,” generate the organization’s base symbol from the preceding name and append “.X” in uppercase; do not treat an internal occurrence of “Class” as a share-class suffix.

items.expected: Synthetic ticker policy: (1) When generating a base ticker, remove leading articles, legal/entity suffixes, and standalone conjunctions; then concatenate the initials of the remaining significant tokens in uppercase. (2) When a name has only one significant token after filtering, use the first four normalized letters of that token as the ticker, or the entire token when it has four letters. (3) When an organization name includes a trailing share-class designation, generate the base ticker from the organization name and append a period followed by the class letter. (4) Normalize punctuation and diacritics before deriving token initials: hyphens and apostrophes do not create ticker positions, and accented initial letters are reduced to their unaccented Latin equivalents. (5) For a significant token containing digits, contribute one character representing the token: preserve a single digit when present, and for a multi-digit numeral use its leading digit. (6) Keep the resulting base ticker compact, with the observed outputs ranging from two to four characters; do not truncate a four-character result formed from four significant tokens.
